- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated continuation; cap forecast increase to 3–5% max for next period.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.5) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; use 1–2 day lagged sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts above 70–75% of recent high, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with historical mean reversion behavior.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); apply 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive and price is trending upward.
